actions.description: Write one 32-bit data word into the FIFO in the write clock domain.

blocking.description: If true, wait until the FIFO accepts the write (full low). If false, attempt only when full is low at the next sampling edge; if full, record a blocked attempt and return without writing.

preconditions: If blocking=true, the testbench permits waiting until full is low.
postconditions: If blocking=true, exactly one word is accepted and written to the FIFO memory; accepted_writes increments by 1.
If blocking=false and full was low at the sampling edge, one word is accepted; otherwise no write occurs and full_write_attempts increments by 1.
The expected data queue in the scoreboard is updated only for accepted writes.
i_wr_en is deasserted after the operation completes.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_write_single(input bit [31:0] data, input bit blocking); Domain: write clock i_wr_clk. Drive on falling edges, sample on rising edges. On entry, deassert i_wr_en if currently high from this task (wait one falling edge to ensure clean state). For blocking=1: wait until a falling edge where o_fifo_full==0 and i_wr_rst_n==1; then set i_wr_en=1 and i_wr_data=data on that falling edge; hold through the next rising edge (accepted if full==0 and reset high); deassert i_wr_en at the following falling edge. For blocking=0: at the next falling edge, set i_wr_en=1 and i_wr_data=data; at the following rising edge, if o_fifo_full==0 and i_wr_rst_n==1, the write is accepted; if full==1 or reset low, no write occurs and increment full_write_attempts; deassert i_wr_en at the next falling edge. If reset becomes active during the operation, abort without incrementing accepted_writes and treat as blocked attempt if non-blocking, or error if blocking timeout. Blocking wait upper bound: 100000 write clock cycles; if exceeded, report a timeout error and abort.

actions.description: Read one 32-bit data word from the FIFO in the read clock domain.

blocking.description: If true, wait until the FIFO has data (empty low). If false, attempt only when empty is low at the next sampling edge; if empty, record an empty read attempt and return without reading.

preconditions: If blocking=true, the testbench permits waiting until empty is low.
postconditions: If blocking=true and not empty, exactly one word is read; accepted_reads increments by 1; the scoreboard pops the oldest expected word and compares o_rd_data after the registered RAM update delay.
If blocking=false and empty was low at the sampling edge, one word is read; otherwise no read occurs and empty_read_attempts increments by 1.
i_rd_en is deasserted after the operation completes.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_read_single(input bit blocking); Domain: read clock i_rd_clk. Drive on falling edges, sample on rising edges. On entry, deassert i_rd_en if currently high from this task. For blocking=1: wait until a falling edge where o_fifo_empty==0 and i_rd_rst_n==1; then set i_rd_en=1 on that falling edge; hold through the next rising edge (accepted if empty==0 and reset high); deassert i_rd_en at the following falling edge. For blocking=0: at the next falling edge, set i_rd_en=1; at the following rising edge, if o_fifo_empty==0 and i_rd_rst_n==1, the read is accepted; if empty==1 or reset low, no read occurs and increment empty_read_attempts; deassert i_rd_en at the next falling edge. Data comparison: after an accepted read, wait #0.001 (timescale 1ns/1ps) after the rising edge, then compare o_rd_data to the queue head; mismatch is an error. Blocking wait upper bound: 100000 read clock cycles; timeout error.

actions.description: Write a burst of n_words sequential data words (start_data, start_data+1, ... modulo 2^32) into the FIFO, with optional gap cycles and blocking behavior.

n_words.description: Number of write requests to issue.

start_data.description: First data word; subsequent words increment by 1 (32-bit wrap-around).

blocking.description: If true, each word waits until accepted (full low). If false, each word attempts once and skips if full.

gap_cycles.description: Number of write clock cycles to wait between consecutive write requests after deasserting enable. 0 means continuous enable (back-to-back requests, no deassert between words).

preconditions: If blocking=true, ensure sufficient time to complete n_words unless timeout.
postconditions: For blocking=true, all n_words are accepted (unless a timeout occurs); accepted_writes increments by n_words.
For blocking=false, accepted_writes increments by the number of words that found full low; full_write_attempts increments for each blocked word.
The scoreboard queue is updated with accepted write data in order.
i_wr_en is deasserted after the burst completes or aborts.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_write_burst(input bit [31:0] n_words, input bit [31:0] start_data, input bit blocking, input bit [31:0] gap_cycles); Domain: write clock. The task iterates n_words times. For each word, data = (start_data + word_index) % 2^32. If gap_cycles==0, the enable remains asserted continuously between accepted words (or between attempts if non-blocking and full? For non-blocking, if full, that attempt is skipped and no enable is asserted for that cycle; but if gap_cycles==0 and non-blocking, the task should still deassert enable after a blocked attempt and then immediately attempt next word at the following falling edge, effectively one cycle gap). For gap_cycles>0, after each word attempt (accepted or blocked), deassert i_wr_en and wait gap_cycles rising edges of i_wr_clk before the next attempt. Blocking wait per word: maximum 100000 cycles. On reset assertion during burst, abort remaining words and report a timeout/error as appropriate.

actions.description: Read a burst of n_words from the FIFO, with optional gap cycles and blocking behavior.

n_words.description: Number of read requests to issue.

blocking.description: If true, each read waits until not empty. If false, each read attempts once and skips if empty.

gap_cycles.description: Number of read clock cycles to wait between consecutive read requests after deasserting enable. 0 means continuous enable.

preconditions: If blocking=true, ensure there is sufficient data or time to complete n_words.
postconditions: For blocking=true, all n_words are read (unless timeout); accepted_reads increments by n_words; scoreboard pops n_words and compares data.
For blocking=false, accepted_reads increments by successful reads; empty_read_attempts increments for each empty attempt.
i_rd_en is deasserted after completion.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_read_burst(input bit [31:0] n_words, input bit blocking, input bit [31:0] gap_cycles); Domain: read clock. Similar to read_single but repeated n_words times. For gap_cycles==0, keep i_rd_en asserted continuously between accepted reads (or between attempts for non-blocking). For data checking, each accepted read pops the scoreboard queue and compares o_rd_data after 0.001 time unit delay. Blocking wait upper bound 100000 cycles per word.

actions.description: Assert and release the write domain reset (i_wr_rst_n) while the read domain continues running.
preconditions: No other write-domain operation from this testbench is currently in progress (enable should be deasserted).
postconditions: Write pointer logic (wptr_full) and read-to-write pointer synchronizer are reset: binary write pointer and Gray write pointer go to 0; o_fifo_full initially goes to 0.
The synchronized read pointer in the write domain (o_rd_ptr_sync) and its first-stage register are reset to 0, but the source read pointer in the read domain is not reset.
After reset release, the synchronizer will propagate the current read pointer from the read domain after two write clock cycles; o_fifo_full may change accordingly.
RAM contents are not cleared.
Checker updates its write-side reset epoch and discards any pending write-side expectations for the old epoch; accepted_writes counter is not reset.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_reset_write(); Domain: write clock. Drive i_wr_rst_n low for at least 2 rising edges of i_wr_clk (recommend 5 cycles), then drive high. Ensure i_wr_en is deasserted before and during reset. The task should wait for the reset to be sampled by the DUT (use appropriate clock edges). After release, wait 2 write clock cycles for synchronizer settling before returning (optional but recommended). No effect on read domain.

actions.description: Assert and release the read domain reset (i_rd_rst_n) while the write domain continues running.
preconditions: No other read-domain operation is in progress (i_rd_en should be deasserted).
postconditions: Read pointer logic (rptr_empty) and write-to-read pointer synchronizer are reset: binary read pointer and Gray read pointer go to 0; o_fifo_empty initially goes to 1.
The synchronized write pointer in the read domain (o_wr_ptr_sync) and its first-stage register are reset to 0, but the source write pointer in the write domain is not reset.
After reset release, the synchronizer will propagate the current write pointer from the write domain after two read clock cycles; o_fifo_empty may change accordingly.
RAM contents are not cleared.
Checker updates its read-side reset epoch and discards pending read-side expectations for the old epoch; accepted_reads counter is not reset.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_reset_read(); Domain: read clock. Drive i_rd_rst_n low for at least 2 rising edges of i_rd_clk (recommend 5 cycles), then high. Ensure i_rd_en is deasserted before and during reset. Wait 2 read clock cycles after release for synchronizer settling. No effect on write domain.

actions.description: Assert and release both write and read resets concurrently to perform a coordinated reset of both clock domains.
preconditions: Both write and read clocks are running.
No outstanding operations; both enables should be deasserted.
postconditions: Both write and read pointer logic and both synchronizers are reset to zero.
Initially after release, o_fifo_empty=1 and o_fifo_full=0 (after synchronizer settling).
RAM contents are not cleared; old data remains in memory but is not considered valid for the new epoch.
Checker clears its expected data queue and pointer tracking; starts a new logical FIFO epoch; accepted_writes and accepted_reads counters are not reset (they continue accumulating for the test).
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_reset_both(); Drive i_wr_rst_n and i_rd_rst_n low simultaneously (or within a small skew). Hold both low for at least 5 cycles of the faster clock (or at least 2 cycles of each domain if clocks differ, so hold long enough to cover 2 cycles of the slower clock). Then release both high. After release, wait 2 cycles of each clock to allow synchronizers to settle before returning. Any data written before this reset is logically discarded from the FIFO perspective; the scoreboard should clear its queue.

actions.description: Wait for a specified number of write clock cycles without driving any DUT signals.

cycles.description: Number of write clock cycles to wait.

preconditions: i_wr_en is deasserted (if this task was driving it).
postconditions: At least the specified number of rising edges of i_wr_clk have occurred.
No DUT stimulus changes.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_wait_wr_cycles(input bit [31:0] cycles); Domain: write clock. Count cycles rising edges of i_wr_clk; return after count reached. If i_wr_en is currently high from this task, deassert it first and wait one extra cycle before counting.

actions.description: Wait for a specified number of read clock cycles without driving any DUT signals.

cycles.description: Number of read clock cycles to wait.

postconditions: At least the specified number of rising edges of i_rd_clk have occurred.
No DUT stimulus changes.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_wait_rd_cycles(input bit [31:0] cycles); Domain: read clock. Count cycles rising edges of i_rd_clk; return after count reached. Deassert i_rd_en first if needed.

actions.description: Mark the beginning of a verification intent for checking purposes; no DUT stimulus.

index.description: Unique index identifying the intent as mapped in the plan.

postconditions: Checker records a snapshot of current accepted_writes, accepted_reads, full_write_attempts, empty_read_attempts, and other relevant state for this intent.
No DUT signals change.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_begin_intent(input bit [31:0] index); This task only calls the checker hook to snapshot counts/state. It must not drive any DUT input.

actions.description: Mark the end of a verification intent and perform any final per-intent checks.

index.description: Unique index identifying the intent as mapped in the plan.

preconditions: A corresponding begin_intent with the same index has been executed.
postconditions: Checker compares snapshots and performs per-intent assertions (e.g., expected transfer counts, flag observations); any mismatch increments error count and marks this intent as failed.
No DUT signals change.
actions.execution_contract: Imported task signature: virtual task exec_end_intent(input bit [31:0] index); This task only calls the checker hook to finalize the intent. It must not drive DUT.
